principles: User opt-in policy is the only authority to start unattended external hosts.
Automation may launch, watch, cancel, and collect evidence, but review, merge, DONE, and production authority remain gate-controlled.
Every host action must be bounded by explicit paths, command templates, timeout, environment filtering, and visible nextAction.
Fake/local coverage must prove scheduler semantics before real host smoke, and real host limitations must degrade visibly.
dispatch_auto must clarify its relationship to overflow_auto so users have one coherent product path.
drivers: Reduce repetitive cross-host handoff labor while preserving Lattice story/scope/receipt authority.
Prevent unattended external CLIs from expanding scope, leaking secrets, running forever, or silently spending budget.
Support practical parallel development with Claude Code/Gemini/Codex without creating hidden auto-merge or production-DONE behavior.

options.name: manual-only-host-overflow
cons: Does not validate user-requested unattended parallel agent workflow

options.name: default-unattended-auto-runner
cons: Creates high risk of hidden host execution, cost, leaks, and false production claims

options.name: policy-authorized-unattended-scheduler
pros: User controls whether unattended execution is allowed
Allows real host launch, watch, cancel, transcript, receipt, and evidence collection inside explicit limits
Keeps merge/DONE/production authority under existing Lattice gates
cons: Requires policy, capability, runner, scheduler, collector, and docs work
Needs careful smoke coverage for both allow and refusal paths

options.name: overflow-auto-wrapper-only
cons: Leaves old and new semantics ambiguous
Does not provide a dedicated policy/check/watch/cancel product path

rationale: Choose policy-authorized unattended scheduling because it is the only option that gives the user real parallel host automation while preserving Lattice authority, visible refusal, cancellation, and manual merge/DONE gates.

preMortem.trigger: User runs dispatch_auto without policy or with wildcard paths/unbounded parallelism
preMortem.consequence: External host could start outside intended scope or user cannot tell why it was allowed
preMortem.mitigation: dispatch_policy check is mandatory; missing/unsafe policy returns supervised/manual refusal with exact reasons

preMortem.trigger: Runner inherits full shell environment or host CLI sees denied variables
preMortem.consequence: Prompt/transcript may expose credentials or unintended local context
preMortem.mitigation: Runner uses environment allow/deny filtering, records sanitized env summary, and tests forbidden env rejection

preMortem.scenario: Host CLI hangs or spends too long
preMortem.trigger: Claude/Gemini/Codex process blocks, waits for input, or exceeds timeout
preMortem.consequence: Unattended run consumes time/cost and leaves user without control
preMortem.mitigation: Runner enforces timeout/kill and scheduler exposes dispatch_cancel with stopped/cancelled watch state

preMortem.scenario: Mixed worker outcomes hide useful evidence
preMortem.trigger: One parallel worker succeeds while another fails or is cancelled
preMortem.consequence: User loses successful receipt/diff or gets false aggregate success
preMortem.mitigation: Scheduler aggregate remains diagnostic/partial while preserving each worker transcript, receipt, and nextAction

preMortem.trigger: External CLI writes transcript claiming tests passed, receipt verified, or productionDone
preMortem.consequence: Lattice could mistakenly treat host prose as authority evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Collector derives changedFiles from git and hard-codes authorityChanged=false, receiptVerified=false, productionDone=false; gates require local validation/review/delivery/server receipt separately

preMortem.scenario: Entry point confusion between overflow_auto and dispatch_auto
preMortem.trigger: Users see both commands and cannot tell whether one replaces or wraps the other
preMortem.consequence: Product feels unfinished and users choose unsafe/old path by accident
preMortem.mitigation: Docs and smoke require overflow_auto nextAction/migration guidance to dispatch_auto for policy-authorized unattended mode
